body.statement: If the supplied \(\mathcal K\) is a vertex cover of \(C_G\), then all \(F_{\ell,A}(z)\) with \(|A|\le2\) are computable exactly in \(Lk!3^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, and every intermediate rational has bit length \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\).
body.justification: This complete special case evaluates each chamber monomial directly and establishes a genuine fixed-parameter guarantee.
body.gap: Static vertex-cover programs do not assign heterogeneous greedy-order probability.
body.consumer: Experiments whose measured conflict cycles are concentrated on a small vertex-cover hub set obtain an exact fixed-parameter AWRI rule comparison.
body.proof_tex:
Assume that \(\mathcal K\) is a vertex cover, so \(V\setminus\mathcal K\) is edgeless.  If \(k=0\), the whole graph is edgeless, every vertex is selected, and each admissible tagged polynomial is \(z^n\); hence suppose \(k\ge1\).  Fix an independent \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\).  Conditional on \(S_\ell\cap\mathcal K=\mathcal U\), independence forces every vertex of \((V\setminus\mathcal K)\cap N_{C_G}(\mathcal U)\) to be unselected.  Every vertex in
\[
 T_{\mathcal U}:=(V\setminus\mathcal K)\setminus N_{C_G}(\mathcal U)
\]
must be selected: it has no selected core neighbor and, since the complement of the cover is edgeless, could otherwise have no selected neighbor at all, contrary to \(\texttt{lem:greedy-domination-certificate}\).  Hence the only possible output for this core choice is \(S_{\mathcal U}=\mathcal U\cup T_{\mathcal U}\), and the contribution is zero unless \(A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}\).

Apply \(\texttt{prop:core-inclusion-exclusion}\).  For a fixed \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U\), an unselected exterior vertex \(v\) contributes
\[
 \int_0^{p_v(x)}h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\,dy
 =p_v(x)^{h_{\ell v}},
\]
and a selected exterior vertex contributes
\[
 \int_0^{r_v(x)}h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\,dy
 =r_v(x)^{h_{\ell v}}.
\]
Fix an ascending chamber \(0<x_{\sigma(1)}<\cdots<x_{\sigma(k)}<1\).  On this chamber, each nontrivial maximum \(p_v\) and minimum \(r_v\) is one named coordinate, while \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}\) is constant.  Thus the full integrand is either zero or \(\bigl(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\bigr)\prod_{j=1}^kx_{\sigma(j)}^{\alpha_j}\) for explicitly accumulated nonnegative integers \(\alpha_j\le nb\).  Repeated integration from the smallest coordinate upward gives
\[
 \int_{0<x_{\sigma(1)}<\cdots<x_{\sigma(k)}<1}
   \prod_{j=1}^kx_{\sigma(j)}^{\alpha_j}\,dx
 =\prod_{r=1}^k\frac{1}{r+\sum_{j=1}^r\alpha_j}.
\]
This is a direct rational evaluation, not an integration gate.  Add it with sign \((-1)^{|\mathcal B|}\) to the coefficient of \(z^{|S_{\mathcal U}|}\).

There are at most \(k!3^k\) triples consisting of a chamber and a pair \((\mathcal U,\mathcal B)\).  Adjacency tests, exponent accumulation, and tag tests are polynomial in \(n\) and \(\lambda\), and there are \(1+n+\binom n2=O(n^2)\) tags and \(L\) rules.  Put \(D'=k(nb+1)\).  Every chamber-integral denominator is a product of \(k\) integers at most \(D'\), and hence divides
\[
 \Delta=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,D')^k.
\]
Using this common denominator, the accumulated numerator has bit length at most \(\log\Delta+O(k\log(k+1)+n\log b)\), which is polynomial in \(n,b,\lambda\).  Thus every rational operation has polynomial bit cost.  Multiplication by the number of chambers, pairs, tags, and rules gives \(Lk!3^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, while the stronger polynomial height bound implies the stated \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) height bound.  This computes every tagged polynomial exactly.
